A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BFB/RFB research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across reordering and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, context-length and data-diversity ablations, concentration sensitivity, and representation analyses in Sections 3–4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds OGBench Scene results and Contextual-FB and Oracle-ID comparisons in Table 1.

M1.justification: The defining procedures remain: separately trained belief estimation, forward-only context conditioning, and vMF task sampling implemented through Householder reflection. Algorithms 1–2 are substantively unchanged. Newly documented forward-network ensembling and DDPG-style actors do not establish a redesign of BFB/RFB.

E1.justification: v2 Table 1 adds OGBench Scene with friction variation, extending evaluation beyond the retained maze-layout and wind-direction environments to a distinct dynamics-generalization scenario. Randomized-Doors, FourRooms, PointMass, and AntWind coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates Random, FB, HILP, and LAP. v2 Table 1 adds a reimplementation of Contextual-FB and an Oracle-ID comparator to the existing FourRooms, PointMass, and AntWind comparisons, as well as evaluating them on Scene. Contextual-FB was previously discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: The reported discount changes from 0.99 in v1 Table 4 to 0.99 with a maze-specific 0.98 in v2 Table 5. The new Scene evaluation specifies training friction of 0.4–1.0 and testing friction of 0.1–0.3. Existing dataset-generation procedures and training budgets are otherwise retained; these disclosures do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: The new Oracle-ID control probes conditioning on explicit environment identity: it performs strongly on training dynamics but poorly on unseen dynamics. The existing context-length, data-diversity, concentration, embedding, and Q-function analyses remain substantively unchanged.

E5.justification: Figure 1 changes its reported standard-deviation calculation from three seeds to five seeds. Figures 5–6 still report three seeds. This establishes a change in reported run information, without establishing that all experiments were rerun or received additional seeds.

E6.justification: v2 Table 1 adds Scene results and the new comparators' results, including Scene test scores of 0.45 for BFB, 0.55 for RFB, and 0.0 for Oracle-ID. Original benchmark means are reproduced, but uncertainty values differ: FourRooms test RFB is 0.61 ± 0.05 in the new table versus 0.61 ± 0.02 in v1 and the retained v2 Appendix Table 2.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 replaces the bound 2γ||r||∞εk/(1−γ)^2 with 3R(ε*k+Δest)/(1−γ), explicitly introducing estimation/optimization error and revising coverage assumptions. The partitioning result replaces the earlier Gram-matrix argument with an explicit block-separable parameterization assumption. v2 Appendix B substantially rewrites the proofs and expands the successor-measure and Bellman derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: diagnosing dynamics interference in FB, introducing BFB and RFB, and demonstrating adaptation to unseen dynamics. The headline claim of up to twice the baselines' zero-shot returns is unchanged.

C2.justification: v1 interprets increasing approximation error as increasing regret; v2 explicitly limits this inference to the bound and explains that additional data may reduce estimation error. Independence from environment count is now conditional on controlling the largest cluster. v2 also adds reward-representation, convergence, and test-time exploration limitations, while dropping the transformer-cost caveat.

D1.justification: Appendix E revises reported hardware from four 4090 GPUs to one RTX 4090 and adds approximately one hour of total training time. It newly documents forward-network averaging, DDPG-style actors, baseline repository sources, and HILP's use of original hyperparameters. The direct project-code link is replaced by a project-page link.

R1.justification: v2 adds Lillicrap et al. on DDPG and Grillotti et al. and Urpí et al. on exploration-related methods. The main related-work discussion remains similar; Contextual-FB was already positioned as the closest dynamics-adaptation approach, although v2 now evaluates it directly.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, problem statement, and theoretical explanations receive substantial rewriting. The short FB-training summary becomes a structured explanation in Appendix B.1, and proofs move ahead of environment and experimental details. v2 also adds acknowledgments and updates author affiliations and publication text.

P2.justification: v2 adds a main-text table combining train/test comparisons across environments. The original tables remain in the appendix with new numbering, and all twelve figures are retained. Captions, float placement, title styling, and conference headers change, without a substantial redesign of the existing visual evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 improves precision by qualifying v1's regret interpretation and making theoretical assumptions and exploration limitations more explicit. The added comparisons and friction evaluation provide useful evidence. However, sparse documentation of the new experiments, conflicting uncertainties between Table 1 and Tables 2–3, and the unexplained relationship between block separability and the implemented shared backward network limit the overall gain.
